lead: you were twenty-three when you said it, and the sentence was short, and every question that has arrived in the thirty-one years since had already been answered by it before it came.
sun: what you made of the marriage was structure rather than warmth — which house, whose parent came into the front room, what happens to the money if one of you cannot work. all of it was settled early and none of it has been reopened. she has lived inside that arrangement for three decades the way anybody lives inside a room, with nothing in it ever prompting her to consider where the load goes.
moon: the oath does the deciding. her mother's last two years in that room, the move for her job that cost you the yard, the loan to her brother — none of it arrived as a choice, because the choice was made once and covers everything after it. willingness was never in question. nothing in you generates a route out, and you have never gone looking for one.
pull: she has never been chosen twice. the vow decided it, and thirty years have been the vow carried out, which is not the same as being wanted and cannot be told apart from it.
tension: twice, that you know of, she has told somebody that she is well looked after. the words are exact and they are not the ones she wanted. nothing in the arrangement has ever failed her, which leaves no incident to point at and nothing to raise, and what surfaces instead is a flatness at long intervals that clears by the weekend. from outside, thirty-one years reads as devotion and the pair of you get asked how it was done.
cost: three decades have held everything put on them: two years of illness in the front room, both children through, one thin decade of no money. nothing in those years has required you to want any of it. the arrangement asks for performance and does not ask after the person performing, and you have not put that question to yourself either, in thirty-one years of getting up and doing it.

lead: your number in the register is three. one and two are dead, and the paragraph that makes a number mean anything is one you wrote at thirty-one, when it cost you eleven years of waiting.
sun: the co-operative is a document before it is a building — who is admitted, in what order a flat falls to somebody, what happens to a household that cannot pay for a year. you wrote it in a fortnight and it has not been amended since. thirty-nine households have lived their whole adult lives inside its terms without any of them producing an evening on which the terms had to be looked at.
moon: seniority here is a date. two members are older than you and stand behind you, because they came later, and the order was conferred by arrival rather than by anyone's assessment. what it does not convert into is fondness. holding the order is protection if you are near the bottom of the list and obstruction if you are halfway up it, and the act is identical from either end.
pull: the order that puts you first was written by you when it put you last, and there is nobody senior enough left to be asked whether that was decent.
tension: the newer households have a theory, put politely at meetings: somebody drafts a queue and thirty years on is standing at the top of it. the dates are public and settle nothing, since a date is not an argument about motive. what would answer it is the eleven years the paragraph cost you when you were thirty-one and last on your own list, and saying that at a meeting turns it into a plea.
cost: your own daughter waited seven years for a flat in a place you run, and got one when the list said. thirty-nine households have never had to wonder whether somebody was fixed up quietly. she takes that as a paragraph being worth more to you than she is, and holding a line is the one act that cannot be seen to have cost the person holding it.

lead: the library took you in at fifteen and you have kept it running since forty. it was set up for a reason nobody there had questioned, and you went under that reason, and then under the one beneath it.
sun: the subscription terms, who is admitted, what the fund is allowed to be spent on, the lease with another sixty years to run — that is what you hold there, all of it written, none of it needing you twice. it is the material you sit in the middle of every week: a structure of your own making, sound in every part, in plain sight, and never once in question.
moon: you took the origin story down through three plausible versions before reaching the true one, which is smaller than any of them and comes down to a salary. then you went under that, into where the money had come from, because arriving somewhere sufficient has never registered in you as arrival. an examination is a dismantling. nothing you have ever looked at stayed whole while you looked at it.
pull: you can say what that room stands on, layer under layer, and the one structure your looking has never brought down is the one you are holding up yourself.
tension: two people stopped speaking to you over the anniversary booklet, and the elder of them had loved that story since childhood. no part of your account is disputed by anybody, including her. the committee's word for you is thorough, and it is a word for somebody who does slightly more than the job needs. what happened is that no signal ever came to say the question was answered, and no such signal exists in you to come.
cost: there is a shelf of your notebooks in that room, and every question anybody has put about the place in twenty years is answered somewhere in them, further than the question went. what has never been available is the point at which a thing is understood enough to be set down. the room will outlast the story you took apart, and the story will outlast your correction of it.

lead: two hundred of them get to their feet at the same moment every week. the room they do it in stays standing because of you, and the thing that lifts them has never once lifted you.
sun: nothing you look after there happens during the hour it is full. the fabric fund, the rota, the boiler contract, the lease, who holds keys and what the keys open — the enclosure is yours and the event inside it is not. the doors have opened every week for thirty years, including the winter the road was shut, and a body of two hundred has never had to hold a conversation about where it meets.
moon: you move with them and have never been in among them. by the second month you can say which of the newcomers will still be here in three years, and the sorting runs whether or not you want it — the arriving and the leaving read off as one motion, which is a keeper's view of a congregation and not a member's. nobody has asked you for it.
pull: thirty years of keeping the doors open on a thing you have never felt, and somebody in the same seat every week reads as the most devoted person in that building.
tension: the minister before this one asked you in the vestry why you do it, and you told him accurately, and he heard modesty and thanked you for it. that sentence has been said once and landed as its opposite. everything since has confirmed his reading — the seat, the accounts, thirty unbroken years — and the only place left to correct it is a room of two hundred, where a plain statement about yourself arrives as an announcement.
cost: you can name, by the second month, which of the newcomers will still be here in three years, and you are right. the congregation is solvent and has somewhere to meet, in a decade when several around it did not. what none of that has produced is a share in the hour itself, and presence every week is not distinguishable from belonging, so nothing will ever come and ask.
